name: go-tc-actionable-qdisc-extended-acknowledgements
instr:
go-tc cannot identify the typed qdisc option field behind a Linux kernel rejection. Add opt-in extended acknowledgements that correlate kernel offsets with exact wire layouts across scalar attributes, embedded records, raw structures, nesting, headers, and alignment. Preserve existing qdisc behavior when attribution is disabled or unavailable.

Encoding must produce deterministic request-relative field spans without changing emitted bytes. Account for complete aligned records, nested displacement, omitted options, and raw layouts. Across FqCodel, FqPie, Red, Sfb, Sfq, and Cbq, every emitted span must identify the precise caller-visible field owning its bytes. Offsets outside emitted options remain unattributed.

Expose recognized message, offset, and missing-type metadata with explicit presence, ignoring unknown attributes. Attributable mutation failures return an `OpError` with inspectable operation, `ExtAck`, and field path. Its text retains kernel context and its error chain reaches the original failure. Missing, malformed, unsupported, or out-of-range metadata must not hide the kernel failure or invent attribution.

Opt-in behavior must survive copying a `Qdisc`. Add, Replace, Link, Change, and Delete retain their signatures, request bytes, flags, validation errors, successful results, and ordinary cross-platform behavior.
